name: Coverage: every clause has its own scenario
summary: musiccheck.mjs:955-967 pins chord 0 as the verse i chord in both tables; 331-360 finds a single clean seam at a multiple of four no earlier than bar 8; 566-604 freezes the section under each owner.
detail: musiccheck.mjs:385-419 proves the chorus hands the song back only at a seam (exitStep must be 0) and only after CHOR_HOLD bars, reading the hold from the game rather than copying it. 421-466 proves the finale latch reverts the section, re-retunes the oscillators at the same timestamp so the dive's first bar sounds the verse chord, and holds through the dive with heat still hot. 566-604 gives each guard its own tension: armed and rising bars hold the section, a payoff holds it through cooling play, and a black hole holds it too. 516-533 counts snare BODIES per timestamp on level 4 and fails on any doubled slot, which is the drum-slot clause. 535-564 proves all four roads into the chorus work independently and that heat 0.5 does not lift.

name: Coverage: driven for the black hole and the star, absent for pause
summary: musiccheck.mjs:1166-1173 drives bedTick inside a black hole on every level and requires BED.g.gain at or under 0.05; 1326-1336 requires the hypernova star to OPEN the band through the same writer.
detail: The comment at musiccheck.mjs:1319-1325 states the rule the assertion enforces: bedTick is the only writer of BED.g, so a mode that adds voices in musicStep and touches nothing here gets a busier arrangement over a pad sitting exactly where it was. musiccheck.mjs:1356-1383 measures the earned band gain ladder (rest 0.72, earned, peak 1.0) and requires recovery, and 1380-1383 that banked hypernova and spotlight do not change the black-hole mix. NOT ASSERTED: that PAUSE drives bedTick — no harness calls bedTick with PAUSE.on set, so a pause that leaves the pad singing would pass every check.

name: Coverage: the most thoroughly asserted rule in the repository
summary: musiccheck.mjs checks diatonicity at eight separate sites — both chord tables, the drop, the snare, the black-hole piece, the three-act arc, the impacts and the SFX pentatonic.
detail: musiccheck.mjs:971-979 walks both PROG and PROGB and fails any pitch off the semitone grid or outside the natural minor; 986-995 pins each SEVB as diatonic AND a stacked third over the chord's fifth. musiccheck.mjs:1050-1067 requires every pitch fireDrop schedules to be diatonic on every level, and 1068-1088 that level 1's drop is unchanged to within 3 cents of what shipped. 1021-1034 pins the snare body at exactly tonic + 10 semitones. 1138-1155 requires every black-hole voice to be an interval over the tonic; 1454-1460 repeats it across the three-act arc AND enforces the 40Hz floor; 1508-1520 does the same for impacts. musiccheck.mjs:276-298 closes the other half nothing used to check: LV[].key and PROG must agree on the key, or the sound-effect layer plays in a different key from the band.

name: Coverage: death clears seven fields, and the bank is proved separately
summary: musiccheck.mjs:1499-1503 sets pay, brk, brkEnd, a LOOP pattern, a LOOPQ entry and a PLAY.tape row, calls endSection on a dead run and requires every one cleared.
detail: musiccheck.mjs:1178-1194 is the other half: an armed drop entering a black hole must be BANKED as MU.pend and must not remain armed or rising, so the reward outlives the scheduling. dropcheck.mjs:291-293 proves the gameplay side — G.build=2 followed by startGame() leaves no Starfall, no charge and no reward stars. dropcheck.mjs:185-190 resets the same fields at the top of every probe, which is where the list of what a fresh run must not retain is written down.

name: Coverage: three impact kinds and the star overlay are driven
summary: musiccheck.mjs:1508-1521 fires soundImpact for nova, hyper and orbit on every level and requires 4 to 5 voices, at most one drum, all in key and above the 40Hz floor.
detail: musiccheck.mjs:1206-1338 is the overlay proof: the star run must sound every one of its degrees on every level, must deliver about 64 voices against the 64 it owes rather than merely more than a cold bar, must appear in both the square and triangle halves of each pair, and must be outranked by a black hole. fxcheck.mjs:361-367 covers the visual half for eight pickup kinds. NOT COVERED: the other pickups have no audio-cue assertion of their own — soundImpact is only fired for nova, hyper and orbit, so a slip, trail, mirror, scorch or spot pickup that fell silent would pass.

name: Coverage: identity-compared in three states, on every level
summary: musiccheck.mjs:1470-1483 renders each release bar with 0 and with 12 player hits and requires byte-identical output; 1486-1498 requires performerHit identical in ordinary, payoff and drum-fill states.
detail: musiccheck.mjs:1480 also requires the idle render to carry a voice at or above 500Hz, so "identical" cannot be satisfied by silence, and that G.payOpen stays false. musiccheck.mjs:855-862 requires every world to carry a complete 16-step answering phrase with at least four sounded degrees, so no world leaves response bars for the player to fill. 1390-1399 proves the retired tape fields cannot re-enable the recorder: LOOP.pat and LOOPQ must stay empty after a musicStep driven with a populated PLAY.tape. musiccheck.mjs:802-811 requires no MUSIC BUILDS announcement at the chorus transition.

name: Coverage: progression is proved without audio, the reward branch is not
summary: smoke.mjs:66 removes AudioContext entirely and drives the whole game — intro, deaths, levels, black hole, lab, eight viewports — but never earns a Starfall, so runtime.js:1336 is unexecuted.
detail: Running the audio-less harness IS the enforcement of "progression does not block": smoke.mjs:172-1506 plays through every screen with no AC, and any unguarded audio call would throw and fail the run. drawcheck.mjs:226 does the same again over the 2D draw path. musiccheck.mjs:1522-1525 proves an impact scheduled while muted or paused makes no sound. THE GAP IS EXACT: grepping tools/smoke.mjs for starfall, Starfall, dropNeed and build( returns nothing, and dropcheck and musiccheck both install a stubbed AudioContext whose state is running — so the else-branch that hands a muted player their earned Starfall has never once run in CI.

name: Coverage: ordered thresholds and a reachable frontier
summary: check.mjs:284-285 asserts TIERS at: are non-decreasing and LV end: strictly increase; curriculum.mjs:190-248 drives one real climb to LV.length and demands every lesson.
detail: smoke.mjs:343-344 re-asserts at runtime that every tier unlock is finite, non-negative and ordered. curriculum.mjs:189 reads FRONTIER from LV.length rather than a literal, so a new level extends the driven run with no edit. NOT asserted: that a new level's geometry is PLAYABLE — curriculum.mjs:229 only fails when an invulnerable player dies, which no geometry can cause. curriculum.mjs:233-234's TAUGHT list is a hand-written literal, so a newly added formation is only caught indirectly, by smoke.mjs:346 requiring every tier type to own a MEET row.

name: Coverage: partial — the flags are read, the picked-start clause is not
summary: curriculum.mjs:220-244 reads the per-run placement flags at each level card and smoke.mjs:383-388 proves startGame never forges didHop, but nothing asserts a picked start skips earlier introductions.
detail: curriculum.mjs:220-244 samples G.hyperPlaced and G.slipPlaced at the level-2 card and G.spotPlaced and G.trailPlaced at the level-3 card, which proves each orb is REACHED by its home level on one full climb from level 1 — its own comment at curriculum.mjs:211-219 states the honest limit: it cannot tell which branch forced the placement. smoke.mjs:806-821 drives a picked level 3 and checks state, carryScore and score, but never inspects G.seen, G.everHopped or any placement flag on that path. The clause "a selected later start does not owe the introductions belonging to earlier levels" has NO assertion anywhere in tools/.

name: Coverage: the ledger drift guard runs one way only
summary: check.mjs:313-341 collects every TIERS name: and LAB_ORBS n: and fails the build if any is absent from MECHANICS.md, with a floor of 8 names so a broken regex cannot report success.
detail: Matching is case-insensitive substring at check.mjs:333-339 because the code shouts TWIN SHARDS and the ledger writes prose. The check is deliberately forward-only: it catches the failure that happens — a mechanic ships and the row is written "next commit" — and refuses to guess which ledger rows are supposed to name a symbol. check.mjs:520-602 is the companion guard for prose: any document that discusses an ALL-CAPS numeric constant must name that constant's current value in the same paragraph. NOT ASSERTED: that a lesson names a performable action and an observable result — smoke.mjs:359-360's ban on "red kills" is the only content assertion of that kind in the repo.

name: Coverage: the wording is pinned, the ranking is not
summary: smoke.mjs:354-355 requires every tier sub to be the identical string as its formation lesson and 359-360 that no lesson claims red kills outright; nothing asserts message priority.
detail: smoke.mjs:372-376 proves a landed hop cancels the hop rehearsal but not a see-lesson. smoke.mjs:185-186 rejects hazards or difficulty entering the safe introduction, which is the one place danger-versus-teaching is enforced. musiccheck.mjs:809-811 asserts the chorus adds no instruction banner. NOT ASSERTED ANYWHERE: that only one instruction card is live at a time, that immediate danger outranks an ambient announcement, or that two center-screen messages cannot compete. curriculum.mjs:250-259 checks banner ORDER along the ladder, which is a different claim.

name: Coverage: dropcheck owns it, minus the doubling and the muted path
summary: dropcheck.mjs:193-213 proves three fed orbits (two upgraded) and that time, stars, taps, hops and near misses charge nothing; 220-270 proves audible onset, three waves and a hazard-free countdown.
detail: dropcheck.mjs:194-197 feeds 80 rounds of time, ember, hop, tap and small-orbit contributions and requires G.build to stay 0. dropcheck.mjs:220 pins PAY===32 and PAYREST===0; 228-230 requires a finite duration between 8 and 11 seconds rather than 9.23 exactly; 232-233 that the opening blast clears hazards; 265-267 three waves near 3s and 6s. TWO CLAUSES ARE UNASSERTED: nothing checks a Starfall star scores DOUBLE — dropcheck.mjs:241-245 only requires score and ember counts to rise, while the doubling itself lives at runtime.js:8478-8481 — and no harness reaches the muted branch at runtime.js:1325, because dropcheck and musiccheck both install a stubbed AudioContext and smoke.mjs, the audio-less harness, never mentions Starfall at all.

name: Coverage: strong, in the real browser and in the arrangement
summary: enginecheck.mjs:99-114 proves a real pointer tap reverses exactly once and a real touch swipe moves one ring inward in the built app; musiccheck.mjs:1484-1503 proves the verbs never change meaning.
detail: musiccheck.mjs:1486-1498 calls performerHit through judgeTiming in three states — ordinary, mid-payoff and mid-drum-fill — and requires byte-identical scheduled notes and drum counts, which is the direct enforcement of "never remapped". musiccheck.mjs:1390-1399 proves the retired recorder cannot capture or replay a movement phrase, and 809-811 that the chorus issues no instruction banner. smoke.mjs:216-233 drives taps, a swipe and an aborted swipe through the real handlers; smoke.mjs:255-279 proves OS key auto-repeat is not an input, using an ODD burst so the flips cannot cancel out. check.mjs:67-71 fails the build if teaching data mentions the cut echo orb.

name: Coverage: one ladder on the death screen
summary: smoke.mjs:424 asserts LEVEL_MAX === LV.length and 425-445 drives die() at four level/record combinations, then checks the share bar counts the same ladder.
detail: smoke.mjs:430-434 walks FURTHEST YET: level 1 never announces it, a first level-2 death does, a repeat does not, and a level-2 death does not beat a level-3 record. smoke.mjs:435 asserts the retired tier-scale key cometloop:level is never written. smoke.mjs:442-444 requires the share text to read LEVEL 2/LEVEL_MAX with exactly LEVEL_MAX pips, reading the denominator from the table rather than a literal — an earlier version hardcoded /3 and broke when a fourth level arrived. smoke.mjs:787 checks the level picker draws LEVEL_MAX rows.

name: Coverage: eight viewports, every control finite, on screen and disjoint
summary: smoke.mjs:1446-1506 replays the menu, the picker and a lab run on eight viewports from 320x568 to 1280x800 and requires every published rect to be finite, on screen and non-overlapping.
detail: smoke.mjs:1469-1471 requires exactly one each of the start, lab, account and intro controls; 1473 a swipe control; 1481 one picker row per LAB_ORBS entry; 1487 a minimum row height of 18px; 1499 that the lab door is never squeezed below 60px making room for the pause icon. smoke.mjs:748-754 separately asserts the title screen draws start and lab and no retired mode cards, and 757-759 that a tap on the background still starts a run. NOT ASSERTED: anything about the art itself, or that LAUNCH is visually dominant — these are hit-rectangle geometry checks only.

name: Coverage: one harness touches the shipped artifact, and only through the snapshot
summary: enginecheck.mjs is the only check that loads dist/; the other eight run the extracted runtime body in a VM or a virtual document, which is a different surface with a different host.
detail: enginecheck asserts boot, one active scene, one host-owned loop, LAUNCH by published hit rectangle, a real pointer tap, a CDP touch swipe and a portrait/landscape resize — reading only window.COSMO_APP.snapshot() and browser errors. What it does not do: reload the page, trigger SHUTDOWN, sign in, send telemetry, or look at a pixel (that is rendercheck, on a virtual document rather than the built bundle). So the built bundle is proven to boot and respond; nothing proves it tears down.

name: Coverage: NOTHING reads the Capacitor config or any CORS list
summary: No harness opens capacitor.config, checks for a server.url, or compares a function's allowed origins against the two native origins; capacitor appears once in tools/, inside an exclusion regex.
detail: check.mjs:491 mentions capacitor only as a filename pattern inside internalAsset, keeping capacitor*.json out of the published trees — it never reads the file. Grepping tools/*.mjs for server.url and localhost returns nothing else. The Netlify functions are deployed separately from the site and no harness here touches them, so a CORS list that stopped matching capacitor://localhost would break every native cloud call with all nine checks green.

name: Coverage: NOTHING tests the account service
summary: No file in tools/ imports netlify/lib/*, calls merge() or validate(), or drives the account panel; the only account reference in the harnesses is one menu hit rectangle.
detail: I read all nine harnesses at commit 01a3a25. check.mjs mentions netlify only in the pattern that keeps it OUT of the published tree. smoke.mjs asserts the menu draws one account control; enginecheck.mjs:70-76 aborts every off-origin request so no account write can leave the check. plausible.mjs was split out of scores.mjs expressly so it could be checked on a laptop with no network and no blobs dependency — and then nothing was ever written to check it. A broken merge rule, a widened CORS list, a regressed rate bound or an unescaped name would ship with all nine checks green.

name: Coverage: the harness asserts a path production disables
summary: smoke.mjs:1536-1568 proves the play-link self-heal in full, and it can only do so because the VM harness builds the runtime with an empty host where externalLoop is falsy.
detail: It asserts no swap mid-run, exactly one hop from the menu, a ?chk= cache key on the fetch, and that a ?u= URL never redirects again — then prints "play-link self-heal ok". Every assertion is true of the code it runs. None of it is true of the shipped game: CosmoScene passes externalLoop: true, so freshCheck returns at its first line, and the parser could not match a module bundle even if it ran. A reader who meets the harness first will believe the shipped play URL heals itself.

name: Coverage: the proprietary notice is guarded, the third-party file is not
summary: check.mjs:475-476 requires copyright and all rights reserved in the app shell, 512-514 the same in the built dist/index.html, and 500 that public/LICENSE travels with the game.
detail: The built-page check exists because Vite could strip a notice the source carries, so both ends of the build are asserted. THE GAP: public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt appears in check.mjs only at line 493, inside publicAsset, where it is PERMITTED to exist — nothing requires it to be present, non-empty, or to name any dependency. Deleting it would pass every harness, and so would adding a dependency without recording its license.

name: Coverage: both asset trees walked against an allow list
summary: check.mjs:468-469 requires the Pages upload path to be exactly dist; 477-511 walks public/ and dist/ and fails on any symlink, internal file or unapproved extension.
detail: internalAsset at check.mjs:489-492 rejects anything under .git, .env, node_modules, netlify, tools, docs or src, the four uppercase repository documents, package and config files, and every .md, .map, .pem, .key, .p12, .pfx, .toml and .yaml. publicAsset at 493-494 is the allow list: LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt, .nojekyll and a fixed set of image, font, audio, video, json and webmanifest extensions. dist/ additionally permits index.html and compiled assets/*.js or .css (504-506), must contain the Vite entry and a compiled bundle (508-509), and must contain every file public/ holds (510-511). A symlink in either tree fails at 482.

name: Coverage: one live scene is asserted, teardown itself is never driven
summary: enginecheck.mjs:87 and 128 require exactly one active scene after boot and after a resize, and 117-120 that steps and frames track Phaser updates — but no harness reloads or destroys a scene.
detail: enginecheck.mjs never navigates twice, never calls scene.stop or restart, and never re-enters the app, so the shutdown path — listener removal, timer clearing, audio stop, GPU resource release — is executed by no check at all. The closest live evidence is enginecheck.mjs:120, which would catch a doubled render loop IF a second one somehow started inside the single page load. fxcheck.mjs:446-471 covers one adjacent case, a lost GL context handing back to the disc halo, which is resource loss rather than teardown.

name: Coverage: the self-heal mechanism is driven, the release claim cannot be
summary: smoke.mjs:1543-1568 stubs fetch with a newer BUILD stamp and proves the swap happens on the title screen, never mid-run and never twice; nothing checks a published URL.
detail: smoke.mjs:1552-1554 requires no reload while playing; 1556-1560 the swap to /?u=<stamp> from the menu, with the freshness fetch carrying its own cache key; 1562-1564 that a URL already carrying ?u= never redirects again. That is the whole of the mechanism. The rule's actual instruction — verify the deployed build before calling a release live — is a process obligation no harness can discharge, and check.mjs:515-518 deliberately tolerates a missing dist/ so the fast lane can run before a build.

name: Coverage: NOTHING — no harness knows the native projects exist
summary: No harness runs or inspects a Capacitor sync, compares dist/ against the copies inside the native projects, or fails a claim that native source generation is a build.
detail: tools/all.mjs:76-82 builds with tsc and vite before the full suite and stops there; the workflow at pages.yml:27-39 runs npm ci, npm run build, a Playwright install and the nine harnesses, with no native step. Nothing compares the bundled web assets inside a native project against dist/, so a stale sync — the exact failure the ordering rule exists to prevent — is invisible. This rule is enforced only by a reader following CLAUDE.md.

name: Coverage: guarded statically and driven through a real death
summary: check.mjs:265-274 fails if recKey() stops mapping skill to the unsuffixed key; smoke.mjs:761-773 kills a run and requires the record on cometloop:best with no suffixed or mode key written.
detail: check.mjs:230-249 scans every savePref('cometloop:...') literal against a known list and fails on any NEW persisted key, with a floor so a broken scan cannot pass silently; 254-258 requires recKey('best') and recKey('gl') to still have call sites, since those two keys are built rather than written literally. smoke.mjs:432 asserts the level record reaches cometloop:gl at death and 435 that the retired cometloop:level is never written; 769-772 that neither a chill-suffixed record nor cometloop:mode appears; 773 that G.best is the mode's own record.

name: Coverage: the pin, the calm board and the exit are all driven
summary: smoke.mjs:1102 asserts dl() equals LAB_DL, 1148-1149 that neither tier nor level moved in two minutes, and 1240-1243 that leaving clears LAB.on and the lab door.
detail: smoke.mjs:1157-1159 reads the shard cap back out of the game with the black hole neutralised rather than hardcoding it, so retuning LAB_DL retunes the guard. smoke.mjs:1279-1280 requires that leaving a live lab run leaves BH.phase at 0 — no black hole ticking under the picker. smoke.mjs:1435-1437 requires enterPowerSel to clear mirror, scorch, slip, slipFx and the burn buffer. smoke.mjs:1255-1272 sweeps every LAB_ORBS row for 45 seconds each and requires the run never to end by itself, which is the pinned clock proved once per orb. curriculum.mjs:138-149 documents why the curriculum run must never enter the lab: a walk at a frozen dl would never unlock a tier.

name: Coverage: the strongest single guard in the repository
summary: smoke.mjs:1091-1219 empties localStorage, plays a real two-minute lab session with hops and taps, then fails on any key that reappears or any record, flag or counter that moved.
detail: The store is cleared FIRST at smoke.mjs:1091 and the in-memory lifetime flags with it at 1092, because the first version compared before/after on an already-populated store and missed three writes that rewrote 1 over 1. smoke.mjs:1129-1141 plays the session through the real handlers — hops and pointer taps, not a snapshot — because the leaked writes hang off gameplay verbs. smoke.mjs:1192-1213 forces a lab death with every record set so it WOULD move, then checks newBest, best, newLevel, lvlMax, struggle, share eligibility, G.seen, G.runs and the three lifetime flags. 1214-1219 compares the whole store as a map. check.mjs:209-258 is the static complement: a NEW savePref key anywhere in source fails the build, covering the two paths smoke cannot reach, since tryLand and judgeTiming both return early without audio.

name: Coverage: static identity in check.mjs, live wiring in smoke.mjs
summary: check.mjs:169-207 proves skill is the neutral row and every knob has a call site; smoke.mjs:654-733 injects a synthetic mode and proves each knob actually moves its curve.
detail: check.mjs:185-197 asserts every skill knob equals its neutral element (0 for the additive shields, 1 otherwise) and that MD().<knob> has a call site in comment-stripped source; 198-206 that every row carries the same knob set. smoke.mjs:663-710 measures dl, speedAt, warnTime, shardCap, spawnGap and the shield bank through a probe row, then re-measures at MATCHED dl (683-703) so each trim is proved separately from the clock. smoke.mjs:722-727 and curriculum.mjs:273-290 both assert a mode cannot move the tier ladder or a level finish line. smoke.mjs:730 requires the probe torn down and exactly one mode left. NOT ASSERTED: that a mode changes no MUSIC or SCORE rule — neither appears in any mode assertion.

name: Coverage: both directions driven through the real picker
summary: smoke.mjs:822-835 kills a picked level-3 run and requires no FURTHEST YET, no record move and no storage write, then proves a run that began at level 1 and reached 3 still counts.
detail: smoke.mjs:810-814 presses the real picker row for level 3, asserts G.startLevel is 3 and scans the whole store for any key matching lvsel, startlevel or :lv — a persisted pick fails the build. smoke.mjs:821 requires a picked start to carry no previous score. smoke.mjs:842-846 requires the default run's share text to carry no qualifier and a picked run's to say "from L3". This invariant is fully covered.

name: Coverage: the priority ladder in GL calls, the no-flash rule in pixels
summary: fxcheck.mjs:327-377 drives a real orbit, a drop, a pickup and a black hole and asserts the uAccent envelope's onset, magnitude and rank; rendercheck.mjs:323-352 measures the same on rendered frames.
detail: The new assertions are the interesting ones. fxcheck.mjs:342-343 requires an earned transition to be under 0.15 at 0.18s — a gradual onset, not a hit — and 345-347 that a duplicate cue restarts neither the transition nor an impact; 348-350 that it completes by 0.9s. rendercheck.mjs:326-327 fails if a beat impulse alone moves the rendered mean at all; 328-331 requires earned orbital pressure to be visible yet under 1.30x the resting world; 332-334 requires the living field to move at least 0.20 cell luma across two seconds; 339-341 requires an earned event to stay inside a 0.84-1.16 luma ratio while still deforming the field by 0.20 — that pair is the "motion and material, not a flash" clause made measurable. musiccheck.mjs:1598-1622 covers it from the audio side across four passages: beat timestamps must drain with G.beat and BEATQ left at zero while music keeps sounding. Priority and expiry: fxcheck.mjs:351-359 and rendercheck.mjs:344-351.

name: Coverage: the deepest GL coverage in the repo, minus kernel normalization
summary: fxcheck.mjs:234-286 checks uniform names, null writes, non-finite values, six render targets at three scales, eight draws per frame and the upload Y-flip; 446-525 covers lost context and edge pileup.
detail: The recording fake parses uniform declarations out of the shader it was handed (fxcheck.mjs:48 and 66-69) and returns null for anything else, reproducing real WebGL exactly; 250-255 additionally requires every looked-up location in GL.u, FX.uB and FX.uC to actually be WRITTEN. fxcheck.mjs:446-471 kills the context mid-run and requires FX.on false, bloomHalo true and no further draws into the dead context. 473-525 parses the shipped kernel constants and simulates the 1-D chain with the source's real sampling semantics, failing if the border gain exceeds 1.05. rendercheck.mjs:219-243 measures the rim on real pixels and 245-285 pins the glow-to-disc light ratio between 0.35 and 2.6. NOT ASSERTED: that the blur kernel sums to 1, and that blur offsets are physical rather than CSS pixels — both constants are parsed and used, never validated.

name: Coverage: the harness suite polices its own membership
summary: check.mjs:361-377 fails if any tools/*.mjs is missing from pages.yml or vice versa, 383-403 if one declares no @lane or seeds without printing the seed, 434-452 if docs/harnesses.md never names it.
detail: all.mjs:29-30 parses the workflow and runs exactly CI's steps rather than holding a list, closing the loop from the other side: a harness cannot be in the tree without running in CI, and cannot run in CI without running locally. check.mjs:461-464 fails the build if pages.yml runs rendercheck without installing a browser, since a silent SKIP would remove the only pixel check; rendercheck.mjs:89-95 makes a missing Playwright a hard failure in CI and a loud skip elsewhere. drawcheck.mjs:359-363 requires each of its four phases to have issued at least 200 draw operations, so no assertion can pass by grading an empty canvas. All nine harnesses are wired at pages.yml:31-39 and named in docs/harnesses.md. Note the lane split has drifted from its own prose: all.mjs:45-49 still describes four fast and four slow harnesses, and there are now four fast and five full. UNENFORCEABLE: the clause asking a human to inspect a real frame.

name: Coverage: eight worlds in pixels, and the built host now counts its materials
summary: fxcheck.mjs:534-563 validates the eight-world table and every morph between them; rendercheck.mjs:294-318 renders each in Chromium; enginecheck.mjs:89-90 requires three GPU materials in the built app.
detail: enginecheck.mjs:89-90 is new and closes the art-asset half that was previously untested: the built Phaser host must report background.gpu true and exactly three materials handed to the GPU background. fxcheck.mjs:537-538 fails if the journey loses a named destination or gains a duplicate; 539-544 requires every scalar finite and every dimension positive; 549-562 walks 100 interpolation steps per world, renders each, and requires the boundary jump to stay under 1e-8. rendercheck.mjs:311-316 fails only when two worlds collapse in BOTH hue and spatial composition, which lets near colours coexist with different silhouettes. rendercheck.mjs:357-376 renders drawCalmSky and requires the 2D fallback within 16% of the GPU cloud light; fxcheck.mjs:584-599 proves the no-GPU path runs the disc halo and issues no GPU calls. NOT ASSERTED: that an opaque plate cannot replace the scene — nothing reads public/art/manifest.json or checks a texture's alpha.

name: Coverage: NOTHING — every harness pins the preference off
summary: All six VM harnesses stub matchMedia as () => ({ matches: false }), so the reduced-motion branch has never executed in any check, and neither browser harness emulates the preference.
detail: The stub is identical in smoke.mjs:53, dropcheck.mjs:81, curriculum.mjs:59, musiccheck.mjs:146, fxcheck.mjs:149 and drawcheck.mjs:213, and each sandbox re-exposes it through window. rendercheck.mjs launches Chromium with no reducedMotion context option, and enginecheck.mjs:68-69 creates its context with viewport, deviceScaleFactor, hasTouch and isMobile only. Every assertion about cues, labels and envelopes in this repository was therefore made with motion at full. A reduced-motion path that dropped a cue entirely, or threw, would pass all nine harnesses. Playwright supports this directly — newContext({ reducedMotion: "reduce" }) — so the cheapest fix is a second pass in rendercheck.

name: Coverage: a static prohibition, a live uniform, and real captured draw positions
summary: check.mjs:131-141 fails if any ember or orb is given a second radius; fxcheck.mjs:574-580 compares the GPU arena band against radiusOf and AY; smoke.mjs:1381-1411 captures actual draw coordinates.
detail: smoke.mjs:1381-1411 was rewritten in commit 01a3a25 and is now much stronger than the source-regex it replaced: it wraps bloomDot, artifactStar and the canvas path calls, runs a real draw() with two captured magnet/trail stars, and requires the body, the bloom and the route stroke to all land exactly on starVisualPos — the old version asserted source formatting and rejected legitimate fade code. The static guard at check.mjs:131-133 matches on an OPERATOR rather than a bare name so a comment explaining the removal does not fail the build, and covers s, st, sp, ts, pw, nn, st2 and st3. fxcheck.mjs:578 requires the uniform to equal [radiusOf(0)/H, radiusOf(nRings-1)/H, AY] within 1e-10 at 2, 3, 4 and 5 rings. smoke.mjs:559-564 requires every RADII entry to return to its exact pre-black-hole value. NOT COVERED: the camera dolly — no harness compares a background transform against the gameplay transform.

name: Coverage: the numbers cannot go stale, the readability claim is unmeasured
summary: check.mjs:520-602 fails any document that discusses SKY_ARENA_CALM or GL_MOTION without naming its current value in the same paragraph; nothing measures hazard contrast against the sky.
detail: That guard is why docs/invariants.md:95 already reads 1.0: it collects every const NAME = number of five or more capitals from the runtime (check.mjs:540-542), walks every .md in the tree rather than a hard-coded list (553-559), and compares numerically inside the paragraph containing the name (587-595), so prose writing 0.6 for 0.60 passes and quoted history may stay. rendercheck.mjs:302-307 bounds each world's mean, p90, p10 and per-pixel gradient, which keeps a sky from flooding or flattening — but it renders with G.spikes emptied (rendercheck.mjs:123 and 139), so no measurement anywhere compares a hazard against the background it has to be read against.

name: Coverage: every clause driven, the two numbers only symbolically
summary: smoke.mjs:1413-1434 banks charge from an inner-ring dwell, proves suspended powers do not spend, misses the deadline for one shield, and cashes an early escape exactly once.
detail: smoke.mjs:1419-1423 sets slow, spot, hyper, mirror, scorch, slip, a burn cell and a route star, runs update(0.25) inside the mode and requires every one unchanged — that is the suspension clause. 1424-1426 sets BH.t to BH_DUR-0.1 with escape open and requires phase 3, one shield spent and the score unmoved. 1432-1434 cashes an early outward escape and pins the exact payout formula. smoke.mjs:487-503 proves the horizon bonus pays once per mode rather than once per arrival; 549-566 that a successful escape pays and the orbits, ring count and shard cap all come back; 571-592 that a death mid-mode awards no escape bonus. The 12 and 17 are read from BH_ESCAPE and BH_DUR symbolically (smoke.mjs:552, 1424), so retuning either constant silently changes what the prose in docs/invariants.md means with no check failing.

name: Coverage: a locked phone is simulated directly
summary: smoke.mjs:921-927 advances the clock ten minutes without running a single frame and requires pausedSeconds() to have grown by at least 590 seconds.
detail: smoke.mjs:914 first requires pausedSeconds() to exceed 9 after 600 paused frames, so the accumulator is live before the no-frame case is tested. The comment at smoke.mjs:915-920 names the mechanism: frame() clamps dt to 0.05s and rAF does not fire while hidden, so a dt-based accumulator would report near zero. smoke.mjs:944-953 covers the other clock: RESUME starts the count-in, the world does not move during it, frozen() reports true, and the clock restarts afterwards. smoke.mjs:954-958 adds the cooldown so pause-resume-pause cannot be farmed for frozen looks at a live board.

name: Coverage: NOTHING measures pressure per ring
summary: No harness divides hazard count by ring count or by track length; the only density assertions are absolute shard counts against shardCap(), which is exactly the measure this rule warns against.
detail: smoke.mjs:504-505 requires the black hole to raise shardCap() and shorten spawnGap() — both totals, and the mode also opens a fourth ring, which is the confound named in the rule. smoke.mjs:1158-1166 compares a calm peak against calmCap and a mode peak against the same cap, again in absolute shards on a board whose ring count is fixed at 3. smoke.mjs:595-635 tests clearance around ONE comet on one ring, which is a placement rule rather than a pressure measure. Nothing anywhere computes shards per ring.

name: Coverage: the freeze is proved, the input and audio clauses are not
summary: smoke.mjs:899-913 snapshots fifteen fields keyed off G.t and requires every one unchanged across ten seconds of paused frames; 897 requires G.state to stay playing.
detail: The snapshot at smoke.mjs:902-905 covers t, vt, dl(), angle, tier, every shard position and phase, star and orb counts, score, shields, BH.phase, BH.t and the three spawn timers. smoke.mjs:930-937 proves a tap on the paused background neither resumes nor reverses and the keyboard cannot hop through the panel. dropcheck.mjs:275-284 proves a Starfall countdown and its waves do not advance while paused; musiccheck.mjs:1523-1525 proves soundImpact is silent under PAUSE.on. NOT ASSERTED: that held pointer input is RELEASED on pause, that continuous pads are silenced (bedTick is never driven under PAUSE.on anywhere), and that a native or visibility resume does not restart a live run — smoke.mjs:289-291 fires visibilitychange in both directions and asserts nothing at all about the result.

name: Coverage: enginecheck counts steps and frames against Phaser updates
summary: enginecheck.mjs:117-120 requires simulation steps and rendered frames to each track Phaser updates within one, in the real built app; 85-88 pins engine, loopOwner and one active scene.
detail: The assertion at enginecheck.mjs:120 names the failure directly — "a second render loop is active". enginecheck.mjs:123-129 resizes to landscape and requires sceneCount still 1 and the run still live, so a resize cannot fork a second scene. enginecheck.mjs:133-134 requires no runtime draw error and no browser exception. check.mjs:471-474 is the static half: the app shell must have a module entry and must NOT contain a second inline copy of the canonical game.

name: Coverage: asserted against radiusOf, not against the index
summary: smoke.mjs:525-530 requires the black-hole pull to raise the ring index AND to land the comet at a smaller radiusOf than ring 0 — the index and the radius are both checked.
detail: smoke.mjs:536-543 adds the two neighbouring failures: the pull may not bank intervals at the innermost ring, and an outward escape may not be cancelled on the frame it lands. enginecheck.mjs:108-114 proves a real downward touch swipe moves to ringIndex + 1 in the built app. fxcheck.mjs:574-580 requires the GPU arena band to equal [radiusOf(0)/H, radiusOf(nRings-1)/H, AY] at 2, 3, 4 and 5 rings and fails if the first is not the larger. smoke.mjs:470 requires the fourth ring to have a positive radius and 1414-1418 that black-hole charge accrues at ring nRings-1 and not away from it.

name: Coverage: NOTHING asserts it
summary: No harness in tools/ reads src/game/contracts.ts, checks that runtime.js is still JavaScript, or scans any document for an overstated type-coverage claim.
detail: Grepping tools/*.mjs for "contracts", "typecheck" and "tsc" returns only tools/all.mjs:78, which runs tsc --noEmit before the full suite, and tools/check.mjs:491, where the string tsconfig appears inside the published-asset exclusion regex. Neither is an assertion about this rule. tsc passing says nothing about whether a document claims more coverage than exists. check.mjs:520-602 could in principle catch a stale prose CLAIM, but it only fires on ALL-CAPS numeric constants, never on wording.

name: Coverage: suspension, resume and reset all driven
summary: dropcheck.mjs:285-294 opens a black hole over a live Starfall and requires its remaining time and wave number unchanged, then proves startGame clears it and its reward stars.
detail: dropcheck.mjs:275-284 covers the pause case in the same block: countdown and waves frozen, and the resume count-in does not consume the reward. musiccheck.mjs:1178-1194 covers the audio half — entering a black hole with an armed drop must BANK it into MU.pend rather than destroy it, and must not leave it armed as well. dropcheck.mjs:296-323 runs a 40-second cadence probe requiring at least three Starfalls from repeated fed orbits, each released on an even scheduler step and within SPB + 0.16 + one frame of arming, which rules out a silent latch.

name: Coverage: NOTHING checks a telemetry property name
summary: The strings game_level, play_mode and tier-as-a-property appear nowhere in tools/; the only telemetry assertion in the repo is on the level_cleared payload's pause fields.
detail: smoke.mjs:965-978 wraps track(), fires levelComplete() and asserts the level_cleared payload carries pauses, paused_seconds and a numeric seconds — which exists because a cleared level's pauses were reported nowhere, not because it guards a name. Grepping tools/*.mjs for game_level and play_mode returns nothing at all. A rename or a redefinition of any telemetry property would pass all nine harnesses.

name: Coverage: weak — the scenic clock is checked, the choice rule is not
summary: fxcheck.mjs:566-572 proves the backdrop clock advances with G.vt and never teleports across a world change, but no harness checks that a deadline reads G.t rather than G.vt.
detail: fxcheck.mjs:566 sets G.vt to 1e7 and requires uTime to advance by less than 0.1 for a 0.1 step, which covers continuity and precision at long session times. smoke.mjs:902 freezes both t and vt under pause, which proves they move together there but nothing about their roles. dropcheck.mjs:268-269 requires the Starfall countdown to match measured G.t elapsed within 0.15s, which is one deadline pinned to the right clock. NOTHING enumerates deadlines and checks their clock, and nothing would fail if a new timed power started reading G.vt.
